day
Phonosemantic compound. 日 represents the meaning and 寺 represents the sound.
四時也。从日寺聲。

Phono-semantic compound (形聲 /形声, OC *djɯ): semantic 日 (“sun; day”) + phonetic 寺 (OC *ljɯs). The phonetic component however represents a footprint pointing up, which could be linked to the concept of the movement of the sun and hence the passing of time.
In ancient scripts, it had the form 旹, with 之 (OC *tjɯ) as the phonetic instead (as well as a reference to the passing of time). The component 寸 was added later.

evidence.source: Chen Jian, “說「時」,” Bulletin of the Jao Tsung-I Academy of Sinology 4 (2017)
evidence.text: The author reports no secure 時/旹 graph or time-word use in currently known Shang oracle-bone, Western Zhou oracle-bone, or pre-Spring-and-Autumn bronze materials. The earliest known 旹 graph is Eastern Zhou; it was often elaborated with 寺 as a phonetic, yielding 時. The paper cautions that alleged oracle-bone 時 examples are generally misread combinations of 之 and 日. It treats abstract time as the lexical core and says early transmitted texts such as the Shangshu already use the word, while distinguishing that lexical antiquity from the later and disputed emergence of a four-season division.
evidence.title: 說「時」

evidence.source: Chinese University of Hong Kong, 漢語多功能字庫, 時 entry
evidence.text: The entry describes Warring States bronze 旹 as 之 above 日: 之 supplies sound and 日 signals time/day. It reports a Warring States bronze use meaning ‘regularly’ and examples of phonetic loan uses of 時 for 寺, 詩, 侍, and 是 in excavated texts. These are whole-graph phonetic uses, distinct from 之 serving as a sound component in 旹.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 時

evidence.source: Chen Jian, “說「時」,” Bulletin of the Jao Tsung-I Academy of Sinology 4 (2017)
evidence.text: The article surveys senses from abstract time: time/moment/duration, time unit, season or quarter, era, timely conditions and calendrical time. It notes proposed lexical relationships with 待 and with 之, judging the latter more plausible while saying the account need not be restricted to solar motion. It also separates the demonstrative use 時 from the time noun because their usage differs in texts; their relationship remains complex. These are lexical/semantic arguments, not proof that the character graph depicts solar movement.
evidence.title: 說「時」

evidence.source: Chinese University of Hong Kong, 漢語多功能字庫, 時 entry

evidence.source: William H. Baxter and Laurent Sagart, Baxter–Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1 (2014), by-GSR table as surfaced in search results
evidence.field: reconstruction_comparison; entries for 之, 寺, 時
evidence.text: The table lists 時 as MC dzyi, OC *[d]ə (~ *[d]əʔ), ‘time’; 寺 as MC ziH, OC *s-[d]əʔ-s, ‘hall’; and 之 as MC tsyi, OC *tə, with separate ‘go to’ and pronoun/particle entries. Thus the MC readings for 之 and 時 are a comparison within the same reconstruction system, but their OC forms differ. The 寺 and 時 OC forms share material while differing in onset and additional morphology. These comparisons are compatible with proposed sound roles, but do not establish phonetic function or a precise historical correspondence by themselves.

editorial_rules: Write about the character's graphic history; distinguish it from the history of a spoken word.
Separate historical explanation from mnemonics. Do not infer history from modern shapes or readings.
Sources may repeat one another. A source count is not independent corroboration.
Treat Shuowen as a historical account, not automatic confirmation. Its generated English glosses are excluded.
Unrelated word senses may appear in Wiktionary excerpts. Do not merge them into a character origin.
Related-character evidence retains its record_character. Do not silently transfer a traditional form's components to a simplified form.
No glyph image has been visually inspected in this packet. Do not claim to have inspected one.
Explain missing evidence explicitly, especially for Japanese-created characters. A Chinese spelling pronunciation is not evidence for a Japanese origin.
